record.abstract: In vehicular integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks, each service-provider vehicle uses a limited power budget to serve multiple sensing targets and communication receivers. Maximizing the communication sum-rate subject to sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints is nonconvex, and iterative optimization is costly to rerun for every network layout. This paper proposes a graph neural network (GNN)-based power allocation algorithm, termed GNN-ISAC. Concretely, GNN-ISAC addresses the aforementioned problem by considering two distinct edge types in the graph representation, one capturing the inter-provider interference, the other representing the intra-provider power-budget sharing. GNN-ISAC is trained without labels using a sensing-penalized sum-rate loss. We also adapt the weighted mean-square error minimization (WMMSE) algorithm to this problem by introducing a sensing-power reservation step. Simulation results show that GNN-ISAC achieves communication sum-rates close to WMMSE with low sensing-link violation rates and much less computation. It also outperforms an existing heterogeneous GNN and a channel-blind baseline, and generalizes to larger networks without retraining.

record.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) model signals as continuous functions from coordinates to values, but their performance depends strongly on how spectral capacity is allocated. Yet most Quantum INR (QINR) architectures treat spectral components as independent outputs of separate quantum blocks. We introduce the Spectral Quantum Memory Model (SQMM), a memory coupled quantum INR in which sequential hybrid data reuploading layers (bands) communicate through a shared coherent quantum memory register. Each band reads the memory, computes on its own coordinate upload, and writes part of its state back, so later bands can build on the computation of earlier ones. When memory read and write layers are input independent, we prove that the memory state forms an operator valued Fourier series whose support is contained in the Minkowski sum of the initial memory spectrum and the local band spectra. Downstream bands then condition their Fourier coefficients on the spectral content stored by earlier bands, and the memory coupling creates no new primitive frequencies. This theory motivates a spectral memory alignment loss that encourages memory to encode the spectrum expressed by the deployed prefix of the model. Across audio and image reconstruction benchmarks, SQMM improves over compact QINR and INR baselines.

record.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) promise to accelerate discovery by reasoning across the ever-expanding landscape of scientific knowledge. Yet, as the reservoir of knowledge grows, the challenge is no longer access to information but rather the ability to connect it in meaningful, domain-spanning ways. In materials science, where discoveries and new hypotheses emerge from bridging insights across disciplines and demand the integration of concepts from molecular chemistry to mechanical performance, this challenge is especially acute. Neither human researchers nor single-agent LLMs can contend with this torrent of information, with the latter often producing brittle reasoning and hallucinations. To address this bottleneck, we introduce a multiagent framework guided by large-scale knowledge graphs to address the urgent challenge of finding sustainable substitutes for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), a class of synthetic chemicals widely used in industrial and consumer applications that are the subject of increasing regulatory scrutiny due to concerns raised in scientific literature and evolving policy efforts to ban certain PFAS compounds. Agents in the framework specialize in problem decomposition, evidence retrieval, design parameter extraction, and graph traversal, uncovering latent connections across distinct pockets of scientific knowledge that support downstream hypothesis generation for PFAS-free materials. Our ablation studies show that the full multiagent pipeline outperforms single-shot prompting, underscoring the value of distributed specialization and relational reasoning. We show that by tailoring graph traversal strategies, the system can alternate between exploitative searches that focus hypothesis generation on domain-critical outcomes and exploratory searches that surface emergent cross-connections in the broader network. Shown through the exemplar of biomedical tubing, the framework generates sustainable material alternatives to PFAS-based tubing that balance tribological performance, thermal stability, chemical resistance, and biocompatibility. This work establishes a framework that combines knowledge graphs with multiagent reasoning to expand the materials design space and reveal interdisciplinary connections. We showcase several initial PFAS-free design candidates to demonstrate the approach.

record.abstract: Nonlinearities are a key feature allowing nonclassical control of quantum harmonic oscillators. However, when nonlinearities are strong, designing protocols for control is often difficult, placing a barrier to exploiting these properties fully. In this work, using a single trapped-ion oscillator operated in the strongly nonlinear regime of the atom-light interaction, we show how to generate localized multi (two, three, four, and five)-component Schrödinger's cat manifolds using a novel form of nonlinear reservoir engineering. We then specifically select Hamiltonians which allow us to perform measurements on these state manifolds. Our work demonstrates the experimental use of high-order nonlinear processes for control of nonclassical states of a quantum harmonic oscillator, opening up a new toolbox which can be applied to bosonic quantum error correction, computation, and sensing.

record.abstract: A double-transmon coupler (DTC) enables a fast, high-fidelity CZ gate between two highly detuned, fixed-frequency transmon qubits. Moreover, a recently proposed capacitively shunted DTC (CSDTC) realizes a small residual ZZ interaction over a wide flux-bias range around zero flux, eliminating the necessity of static flux biasing while maintaining high CZ-gate fidelity. However, CZ gates with the DTC and CSDTC require baseband flux pulses with large amplitudes, which are vulnerable to pulse distortion and decoherence due to large qubit-coupler hybridization. To address these issues, we experimentally demonstrate a parametrically driven iSWAP gate operated at zero flux bias between highly detuned, fixed-frequency transmon qubits coupled through a CSDTC. Using a simple flux-drive waveform without predistortion, we realize an average gate fidelity of 99.92(2)% at a total gate time of 112 ns. The observed high-fidelity performance is consistent with small qubit-coupler hybridization and small effective ZZ interaction during the gate. Our numerical simulations reproduce the experimentally observed iSWAP interaction rate and effective ZZ interaction, demonstrating the applicability of the theoretical model not only to spectral information but also to time-domain dynamics such as gate operations. These results boost further progress in the research of superconducting quantum computers.

record.abstract: Abstract Single-atom waveguide-QED systems have emerged as a leading platform for demonstrating non-linear optics in the few-photon regime. Devices with such non-linear behavior are necessary for developing deterministic gates for photonic quantum computing. Artificial atoms coupled to nanophotonic or superconducting waveguides can be used to engineer highly efficient light-matter interfaces for such non-linear interactions, where every photon in the system interacts with the quantum emitter. However, it has been a challenge to access the reflection port of the waveguide due to the inability of rejecting stray electromagnetic fields that do not interact with the artificial atom. Here, we show coherent reflection of single photons from a semiconductor quantum dot strongly coupled to the fundamental waveguide mode of a nanowire. We utilize the tapered end of the nanowire for ideal mode-matching in a vertical geometry, enabled by the extinction technique developed. This mode-matching allows for efficient transfer of photons from the input to the reflection port while having all interacted with the quantum dot. Such a high-efficiency scalable photonic platform opens up applications in few-photon quantum nonlinear optics and has been proposed for creating key resource states for universal photon-based quantum computing.

record.abstract: Deep learning models for brain tumor MRI classification are usually compared by accuracy alone, on public datasets whose independence is rarely checked. record.abstract: Digital Twins are evolving from passive virtual representations into closed-loop systems that continuously synchronize with physical assets and drive real-time decisions. Yet predictive modeling, machine learning (ML), uncertainty quantification (UQ), and decision-making have been studied as separate capabilities, leaving limited understanding of their integration and maintenance during online operation. This narrative review, scoped by the functional requirements of real-time decision-making rather than by Digital Twin terminology alone, examines how such decisions are generated and sustained in engineering Digital Twins. We first examine foundational decision-making architectures and representative engineering applications, followed by methods that address their limitations across the decision loop. We identify optimization-based, policy-based, and knowledge-based approaches as the major pathways from virtual representation to action. Across them, ML plays three roles in decision-making: enabling efficient surrogate modeling, transforming heterogeneous physical feedback into decision-relevant information, and accelerating or directly generating decisions. UQ supports uncertainty-aware decisions and model adaptation, while continual validation, drift detection, and adaptation help maintain reliable operation as the physical system evolves. Together, these findings underscore the need for a shift from a model-centric to a system-centric perspective on Digital Twins, where its performance depends on the interactions with sensing, state estimation, computation, decision-making, and adaptation rather than on their standalone performance. Therefore, future research should shift from isolated algorithm development toward system-level co-design, scalable decision-making, and approaches to design, and data-efficient continual adaptation and validation for AI-enabled autonomous systems.

record.abstract: This paper presents a distributed model predictive control (MPC) architecture for collision-avoiding motion planning of planar robots with double-integrator dynamics. To reduce coordination demands, a time-varying predicted conflict graph selects relevant pairwise interactions. The associated collision-avoidance constraints are convexified once per MPC update using warm-start trajectories, yielding a fixed convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting QP is then decomposed using an edge-consensus formulation of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), enabling parallel robot-local optimization and independent closed-form projections onto separating half-spaces. Execution is selectively supervised by a centralized high-order control barrier function (HOCBF) QP when the distributed candidate does not satisfy the direct-execution conditions. Evaluated in C++ simulations involving 8, 16, and 32 robots, the proposed architecture achieves collision-free execution and substantially improves computational scalability while maintaining task-level performance comparable to a centralized complete-graph baseline.

record.abstract: On 28 April 2025, the Iberian power system collapsed after a rapid voltage rise that led to widespread generation disconnections and loss of synchronism. The final report of the ENTSO-E Expert Panel attributes the blackout to several interacting factors including ineffective voltage control, fixed power factor operation, misaligned protection settings, manual shunt reactor switching, and limited observability. These factors raise a general question: given the current state, can the next trip, ramp, topology action, or shunt switching raise the voltages measured by overvoltage relays above their settings before voltage controls respond? We answer this with a protection-aware dynamic voltage security assessment. For each candidate event, the method computes the voltage at every overvoltage relay over the relay time window from a dynamic model of the network, its controls, and its relays. It predicts which relays trip after a first trip, identifies assets whose relay or measurement data are insufficient for a safety conclusion, and, when one exists, computes a minimum-cost fast reactive power action that keeps all relay voltages below their settings. Case studies on four benchmark systems and a 2000-bus system that reproduces the mechanism of the Iberian blackout show that the method flagged every event that caused a secondary trip within the relay window, never declared safe a plant that tripped within that window, and, on the benchmarks, found fast reactive power actions that prevented the trips within the relay window whenever it judged such actions feasible. These results were validated with nonlinear time-domain simulations. The implementation code and a visual guide of this work are publicly available.

record.abstract: Observation of the quantum Mpemba effect has spurred much interest in its enabling conditions and its relation to the classical counterpart. Here, we consider weakly open many-body quantum systems initialized in different thermal states and examine when the initially farther state relaxes to the (non-equilibrium) steady state faster. We claim that the number of conserved quantities in the unitary part plays a crucial role: the Mpemba effect is possible only when the Hamiltonian commutes with other extensive operators or is integrable. The reason lies in the dynamical evolution happening in spaces of different dimensions. When energy is the only approximately conserved quantity, dissipation pushes the dynamics within a single-parameter manifold of different thermal states. In contrast, for Hamiltonians with several conserved quantities, the dynamics drift in the multi-dimensional space of generalized Gibbs ensembles, whose distance to the steady state is less trivial. We provide numerical results for large system sizes using tensor networks and free-fermion techniques, thereby supporting our claim.

record.abstract: Learning and optimal control under robust Markov decision processes (MDPs) have received increasing attention, yet most existing theory, algorithms, and applications focus on finite-horizon or discounted models. Long-run average-reward formulations, while natural in many operations research and management contexts, remain underexplored. record.abstract: Abstract Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.

record.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-supported telemedicine may extend clinical expertise to rural communities, yet its benefits can be offset by unequal connectivity, digital literacy, data representation, and institutional readiness. This study examined the efficacy and health-equity implications of AI-powered telemedicine in post-pandemic rural Indonesia. A qualitative-dominant, convergent mixed-methods secondary study integrated reflexive thematic analysis of peer-reviewed qualitative evidence and Indonesian policy documents with descriptive synthesis of verified national and clinical datasets. Evidence included 2023 national internet statistics, a 63,012-person chronic-disease survey, a 311-patient rheumatology survey, and a 15-interview qualitative study. Telemedicine was most effective for stable follow-up, medication management, specialist access, and travel-cost avoidance, but was less reliable for first diagnosis, unstable disease, and examination-dependent care. Rural internet use (59.33%) remained 17.47 percentage points below urban use (76.80%). Among people with hypertension and/or diabetes, 98.0% reported no telemedicine use, indicating a substantial implementation gap. Four integrated themes emerged: conditional clinical efficacy, redistributed rather than eliminated access burdens, algorithmic amplification of structural disadvantage, and the necessity of human-mediated hybrid care. Conclusion: AI-powered telemedicine is neither inherently equalizing nor intrinsically exclusionary. Its equity effect depends on assisted access, low-bandwidth design, representative validation, clinician oversight, interoperability, and disaggregated monitoring.

record.abstract: Looped transformers apply a shared block several times per token to improve accuracy without adding parameters. For models such as Ouro that keep a separate key-value (KV) cache per loop, cache memory limits the batch size that amortizes repeated weight reads. Uniform-bit quantization and fixed rules per loop do not allocate precision according to each layer's sensitivity in each loop. Measurements on Ouro show that quantization sensitivity varies across (loop, layer) cells, and the sum of individual cell damages approximates the overall output damage. Sharing damage also varies by cell, with later loops generally tolerating sharing better. Skipping low-attention values to save reads produces errors that compound across loops. LoopKV uses a one-time offline profile to choose 4-bit storage, 2-bit storage or reuse of the final loop's KV for each cell. The planner minimizes reads under budgets for predicted damage and storage. During decoding, each loop reads the high 2 bits of each 4-bit value and fetches the low bits only where its own attention weights require 4-bit precision. A single fused kernel in vLLM executes the plan. Serving Ouro-1.4B on one RTX PRO 6000, the memory-optimized LoopKV-M plan stores 35% less KV than uniform 4-bit quantization (KIVI-4) on the same fused kernel and CUDA graph. It sustains 1.7-2.2x KIVI-4's goodput under a latency service-level objective with a 16K-token maximum length. None of its averages on six public benchmarks falls significantly below BF16's.

record.abstract: Generative world modeling from large-scale visual data offers a promising path toward scalable robot manipulation. By extending visible-surface object flow to the full object geometry, this representation makes complete object motion explicit and applies uniformly to both rigid and deformable objects. We then train a world model that takes an image and a task description as input and predicts dense full-object flow over the reconstructed object geometry. record.abstract: Q-learning has been empirically observed to exhibit substantial transient error. This transient remains uncaptured by the leading Gaussian limit because the central-limit normalization removes the smaller-scale displacement generated by the initial nonlinear evolution. On the other hand, worst-case finite-sample guarantees, while accounting for transient effects, can obscure the mechanisms responsible for the error on a particular problem instance. We develop a finer asymptotic analysis that gives an asymptotically exact characterization of this transient for a fixed instance. Specifically, for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes, we separate the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization. The centered TD component has Gaussian fluctuations at scale $n^{-1/2}$, whereas the maximization transient is of order $n^{-1}$ and converges almost surely, after rescaling by $n$, to a random limit. This limit represents the propagated effect of maximization errors generated before the greedy policy stabilizes. We combine this characterization with an Edgeworth expansion of the TD component to identify the corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuations, and maximization. The results reveal how transient errors arise for individual Q-learning instances and how their effects persist below the central-limit scale.

record.abstract: Gravitational-wave data is never analysed without some conditioning: filtering and tapering act multiplicatively on the noise, destroying the stationarity on which the Whittle likelihood --- the backbone of nearly all gravitational-wave inference --- rests. The problem is particularly evident for LISA, where gaps are expected to overlap almost all signals and the noise must be estimated jointly with those astrophysical signals. We provide an analytical and numerical framework to assess the impact of noise mis-modelling when signal and noise parameters are inferred jointly in the presence of gaps. From a Fisher-matrix formalism verified against Bayesian inference, we obtain closed forms for the model uncertainties, their maximum-likelihood estimates and the true scatter in the latter, for various approximations to the likelihood. The Fisher-based linear formalism is extended through the Godambe--White curvature to the non-linear regime that severe mis-modelling produces. We survey gap families from long, well-tapered interruptions to short, high-rate ones, injecting massive black-hole binaries. Except in the case of frequent gaps, we show that the windowed covariance is well approximated by its leading diagonal --- the window convolved with the power spectral density --- for the estimation of both signal and noise parameters. By omitting the convolution, the signal sector remains unbiased but the noise parameters, in particular the optical-metrology noise which is dominant at high frequency, is displaced by over an order of magnitude in power. At the highest glitch rates the diagonal approximation stays accurate yet loses an order of magnitude in precision. To remedy this, we propose an exact time-domain likelihood of the surviving samples which can be efficiently (and accurately solved) via preconditioned conjugate gradient methods.

record.abstract: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are powerful tools for analysing time series data that depend on discrete underlying but unobserved states. As such, they have gained prominence across numerous empirical disciplines, in particular ecology, medicine, and economics. However, the increasing complexity of empirical data is often accompanied by additional latent structure such as spatial effects, temporal trends, or measurement perturbations. Gaussian fields provide an attractive building block for incorporating such structured latent variation into HMMs. Fast inference methods for Gaussian fields have emerged through the stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) approach. Due to their sparse representation, these integrate well with novel frequentist estimation methods for random-effects models via the use of automatic differentiation and the Laplace approximation. Scaling to high dimensions requires tools such as (R)TMB to exploit sparsity in the Hessian w.r.t. the latent variables - a property satisfied by SPDE fields but violated by the HMM likelihood. We present a modified forward algorithm to compute the HMM likelihood, constructing sparsity in the Hessian and consequently enabling fast and scalable inference. We demonstrate the practical feasibility and the usefulness through simulations and two case studies exploring the detection of stellar flares as well as modelling the movement of lions.

Conventional high-order methods often suffer from loss of accuracy near curved walls or require complicated wall treatments. To address these issues, in this paper, we develop a NURBS-enhanced $k$-exact finite-volume method for the steady compressible Navier--Stokes equations on hybrid meshes. To incorporate physical wall conditions into the high-order discretization, we develop a wall boundary treatment that employs sequential reconstruction without requiring the reconstruction variables to coincide with those used to prescribe the boundary conditions. The NURBS-based boundary representation is used to obtain a high-order accurate description of curved boundaries, and the diffusive generalized Riemann problem (dGRP) viscous flux is employed to enhance numerical robustness. A variety of numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the high-order accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

record.abstract: The integration of advanced materials and intelligent technologies is transforming sustainable engineering by enabling resource-efficient manufacturing, adaptive systems, real-time monitoring, and improved human–machine interaction. Conventional engineering approaches often rely on resource-intensive materials, energy-consuming processes, and limited monitoring capabilities, creating environmental and operational challenges throughout product life cycles. Advanced materials, including conductive polymers, nanofibers, stimuli-responsive polymers, shape-memory materials, photovoltaic fibers, and flexible electronic structures, offer opportunities to address these challenges through multifunctionality, lightweight design, and improved system adaptability. Concurrently, intelligent technologies, such as embedded sensors, digital monitoring systems, data-driven decision support, and connected wearable devices, support more efficient resource utilization and condition-based operation. Smart textiles provide a particularly relevant example because they combine material innovation with sensing, communication, energy harvesting, and user-oriented functionality. Applications in healthcare, industrial safety, energy management, environmental monitoring, and engineering education demonstrate the interdisciplinary potential of these technologies. However, their sustainable implementation requires careful consideration of material toxicity, manufacturing energy, durability, washability, electronic waste, recyclability, data privacy, and economic accessibility. This paper presents a literature-based technical review of advanced materials and intelligent technologies for sustainable engineering applications. It examines material characteristics, technological integration, application domains, environmental considerations, and implementation barriers. It also discusses life-cycle assessment, circular product design, sustainability-oriented engineering education, and challenge-based learning as complementary strategies for responsible innovation. The review indicates that technological performance alone is insufficient to establish sustainability; environmental integrity, human well-being, economic feasibility, and end-of-life management must be considered together. An integrated framework combining sustainable material selection, intelligent system design, lifecycle evaluation, and interdisciplinary education is proposed to guide future research and engineering practice.

record.abstract: Gene expression is regulated by the targeted degradation of transcription factors through the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Transcription factors destined for degradation are recognized by E3 ubiquitin-protein ligases through motifs termed degrons, embedded within the sequence. In this study, we systematically map degrons in all 1626 human transcription factors. We find thousands of both known and previously unidentified degrons and characterize their sequence properties. record.abstract: The objective of this study to propose a methodology to examine nanofluids flow enhanced thermal conductivity and heat transfer behaviour. The study aims to depict the optimised parameter values at which enhanced thermal conductivity of nanofluids results in more efficient cooling. To achieve this, mixed convection nanofluid (Cu-water) flow over a shrinking sheet under radiative effects is investigated numerically using finite element method (FEM). The analysis incorporates key parameters such as the suction, thermal conductivity, radiation and mixed convection which govern the flow and heat transfer characteristics. The numerical investigation depicts that suction is the most dominant factor which helps to reduce the boundary layer thickness and enhance heat transfer. Radiative effects lead to a thicker thermal boundary layer that consequently reduces the heat transfer rate. The mixed convection parameter also contributes to higher heat transfer rate, simultaneously increasing the skin friction. Corresponding diagrams are plotted to illustrate the outcomes. Results show that the nanofluid model developed in this work exhibits higher Nusselt number as compared to the base microfluid model, confirming improved heat transfer. Also, results obtained statistically by Response Surface Methodology (RSM) using MATLAB® are investigated for optimised value of parameters. The results from the RSM model show a strong positive correlation with our numerical FEM results. The RSM-ANOVA optimisation reveals a strong correlation, giving accuracy of 0.975, highlighting the roles of suction and radiative heat transfer in determining thermal behaviour. This study provides insights for effective thermal management in thin-film manufacturing processes.

record.abstract: Autonomous cyber defense is widely studied with deep reinforcement learning, but most work trains policies inside simulators because learning requires many trial-and-error interactions. Simulator-based training carries a fidelity gap: trained policies face authentication delays, partial action failures, service dependencies, and user traffic patterns that the simulator did not represent, and degrade on transfer. Training directly in the network being defended removes the gap but makes every interaction slow and costly, so sample efficiency becomes the binding constraint. Model-based reinforcement learning has reduced sample requirements on games and physical robots by orders of magnitude by planning inside a learned world model, but it has not been applied to defenders trained in operational networks. We present FOE-Dreamer (Factored Opponent-Enhanced Dreamer), a model-based reinforcement learning framework that trains a defender online and directly in a network on cloud infrastructure, without a simulator stage. FOE-Dreamer separates three sources of variation in the latent state: a controllable component driven by defender actions, an exogenous component driven by benign user activity, and an opponent embedding inferred from defender-observable signals alone. Separating the components reduces the variance in policy gradients during planning in imagination. Against two scripted attacker profiles with user activity emulated by the GHOSTS framework on an 8-host OpenStack testbed, FOE-Dreamer trains within a 3-day budget on a single GPU and achieves about 2$\times$ better episode loss than Rainbow and IQN baselines under matched compute. Both the factoring and the opponent model contribute to the gain, and the learned latents are consistent with the intended separation.

record.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides certified backward reachable tubes (BRTs) for safety-critical robotic systems, but the level-set computation scales exponentially in the state dimension and has historically been performed offline. We present a CUDA implementation of the canonical WENO5 + TVD-RK3 + Lax-Friedrichs level-set Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs solver for 2D, 3D, and 4D dynamics that is fast enough to run inside a robot's control loop. record.abstract: Large language models rely on a single tokenizer that is chosen at training time and fixed thereafter. Most tokenizers are trained on English-dominant corpora, making them under-serve morphologically rich and non-Latin-script languages, where they can produce fragmented representations, longer sequence lengths, and reduced information density during training. We propose Mixture of Tokenizers MoTo, a modular tokenization framework that trains dedicated per-language BPE tokenizers and composes them into a unified superset vocabulary, where tokens shared across languages are deduplicated into a common ID space. Each tokenizer maintains its own normalization policy, pre-tokenization rules, and vocabulary budget. Despite allocating significantly fewer entries to English, MoTo retains English performance while delivering consistent gains across 18 out of 21 typologically diverse languages spanning six scripts, with improvements most pronounced on morphologically complex and non-Latin-script languages that are systematically underserved by English-dominant tokenizer design. Our results suggest that modular subword tokenization is a practical and extensible alternative to monolithic tokenization for multilingual parity.

record.abstract: Adaptive tokenization aims to reduce the compute spent on uninformative image regions while preserving accuracy. record.abstract: Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) requires the calculation of highly accurate electronic-structure energies and nuclear forces at every time step, which can quickly become computationally expensive. Sample-based quantum diagonalization offers a route to such calculations on quantum hardware, but its use in AIMD simulations has so far been limited to active spaces of about 20 qubits. In these spaces, exact diagonalization is tractable, and the quantum circuits are typically built from standard coupled-cluster amplitudes. Here, we introduce SqDRIFT-AIMD, which combines randomized sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SqDRIFT) with analytical nuclear gradients. With SqDRIFT-AIMD, we obtain more accurate ground-state energies than the conventional coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) driven AIMD simulation for the $40$-qubit active space. We apply SqDRIFT-AIMD to study the dynamics of proton transfer in the Zundel cation, using circuits executed on IBM Heron r3 quantum processors. SqDRIFT energies fall below CCSD across the $40$-qubit double-well PES and stay within a few m$E_\text{h}$ of CCSD at 52 qubits. The $40$-qubit SqDRIFT-AIMD trajectory tracks the SHCI-driven proton transfer to within $1.33$ mÅ and exhibits excellent total energy conservation, with a standard deviation of only $0.245$ m$E_\text{h}$. These results extend quantum-centric AIMD to active spaces beyond the reach of exact diagonalization.

record.abstract: In Constitutional AI, a plain-text "constitution" encodes values and gets incorporated into a model via post-training. However, the procedure for creating such a constitution poses significant challenges: who contributes, who decides which norms are included, and to what extent must the process be participatory or democratic? These challenges can be paralyzing. Yet, we argue that taking action is essential: without a deliberate constitution, sovereign models would risk misalignment or default to norms set by frontier model providers. We propose treating the development of a constitution as an evolving, participatory process akin to citizen science, iteratively drafted, tested, and refined. record.abstract: The Boltzmann transport equation describes particle transport across collisional regimes, but resolving its velocity dependence is expensive. Moment methods reduce this cost by evolving finitely many velocity moments, requiring a closure for unresolved higher-order moments. Data-driven closures can represent these moments accurately, yet without structural constraints they may produce complex characteristic speeds and unstable simulations. Learned Boltzmann closures with guaranteed hyperbolicity have so far been formulated in one spatial dimension; in multiple dimensions, hyperbolicity must hold in every direction simultaneously. We develop, to the best of our knowledge, the first data-driven closure for multidimensional Hermite moment systems of the linear Boltzmann equation that is hyperbolic by construction. The network learns a symmetric positive-definite symmetrizer shared by all spatial directions and restricted to a subspace that preserves the known lower-order transport equations; the unresolved rows follow from a symmetric completion. Every directional Jacobian thus has real eigenvalues and a complete set of eigenvectors for every network output and at any truncation order. The closure is trained only on spatial derivatives of unresolved moments from kinetic reference solutions, with no solver in the training loop, and evolved by a partially conservative discontinuous Galerkin method. In two-dimensional experiments in the transition and scattering-dominated regimes, a single learned third-order system with ten moments remains stable in all cases. Averaged over time, it is more accurate than the classical P7 and P15 truncations with 36 and 136 moments in every experiment, and its density error is about two orders of magnitude smaller than that of the P3 truncation with the same moments.

record.abstract: Conventional vector-field-based motion planners for nonholonomic robots consist of two steps: first designing a nominal vector field and then controlling the robot to follow it to approach the target. However, a nonholonomic robot cannot follow the vector field instantaneously and may collide with obstacles, due to the inevitable mismatch between the robot's initial heading and the vector field's direction. This paper proposes a diffeomorphic vector-field alignment (DIVAL) method, which aligns the vector field's direction with the robot's initial heading so the robot can follow the vector field from the start. Specifically, the nominal vector field is locally reshaped by applying a diffeomorphic deformation to the workspace, such that the reshaped vector field has the same direction as the robot's heading at the initial position and coincides with the nominal vector field outside the deformed region. Since DIVAL eliminates the initial heading mismatch, the nonholonomic robot can maintain heading alignment with the reshaped vector field throughout the motion. This heading alignment further ensures that the robot preserves the nominal vector field's properties, including obstacle avoidance, convergence to the target, and smooth control signals. Numerical simulations provide vector-field-tracking baselines where the nominal vector fields are reshaped with DIVAL. Compared to the original baselines, the proposed method achieves collision-free convergence in all trials and avoids control discontinuities. We introduce a methodology that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to distill synthetic knowledge into code. Our system analyzes synthesis routes and translates strategic principles into executable Python functions representing diverse strategic and tactical rules, such as strategic functional group interconversions, protecting strategies and ring construction features. We validate the use of LLM-as-a-judge in this domain, demonstrating their efficacy in evaluating synthesis-specific code generation. By formalizing this knowledge as verifiable code rather than simple heuristics, we create testable, interpretable representations of synthetic strategy. We release the complete codebase and the USPTO-ST data set─synthesis routes annotated with strategic tags. This framework unlocks a novel capability for CASP: natural language-based route retrieval, achieving 74.5% Top-3 accuracy on our benchmark. We further validate our library through temporal analysis of historical trends and chemically intuitive route clustering that offers more granular partitioning than common previous methods. This work bridges the tactical-strategic divide in CASP, enabling specification, search, and evaluation of routes by strategic criteria rather than structure alone.

record.abstract: Residual deployment can affect closed-loop tracking. We compare two ways to deploy one supervised acceleration-residual network in nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) of a quadrotor. Cyclewise deployment repeats one correction across the horizon. Stagewise deployment evaluates shifted prediction nodes before the solve. Network parameters remain fixed during control. On prescribed force pulses, both schemes improve average tracking mainly after force removal, but worsen hover; some prediction checks also fail. Seed 1 reinforcement-learning benchmarks add no mean benefit under pulses or prescribed random forces. On 220 conditions, cyclewise and stagewise supervision reduce mean integral absolute position error (IAE) by 4.38% and 7.77%. On a separate 32-condition bank, fixed gain 1.5 lowers IAE by 27.47% relative to stagewise supervision but raises angular-rate root-mean-square error by 10.19%. In one synthetic computational fluid dynamics field, stagewise supervision lowers four-task mean IAE by 2.01% against a same-graph zero-residual control; some secondary metrics worsen. These simulations show that residual deployment affects tracking, with gains and limitations that depend on task and motion metric.

record.abstract: Mixed-precision quantization, which assigns precisions per-layer, per-network, per-channel, or per-parameter, is gaining traction for efficient Neural Network (NN) realization with higher throughput and lower energy. Unlike conventional fixed-precision accelerators, BF-IMNA advances the mixed-precision design space through an AP-based in-memory implementation. We present BF-IMNA, a bit fluid IMC accelerator for end-to-end Convolutional NN inference supporting static and dynamic mixed-precision without run-time reconfiguration overhead. At its heart are Associative Processors (APs), bit-serial word-parallel SIMD-like engines. We evaluate ImageNet inference with AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50 across SRAM and ReRAM CAM cells, mixed-precision configurations, and supply voltages. To demonstrate bit fluidity, we apply HAWQ-V3's published ResNet18 schedules to the BF-IMNA cost model and pair them with HAWQ-V3's published accuracies and model sizes. The results reveal an accuracy–Energy-Delay Product trade-off. The high-latency point is \(1.16\) points below INT8 accuracy with \(1.13\times\) better EDP, while the low-latency point has \(1.91\times\) better EDP and a \(45.5\%\) smaller model at a \(3.00\) -point accuracy reduction. record.abstract: Underwater acoustic communication faces challenges such as limited available bandwidth and complex channel environments, which impose demanding requirements on efficient image transmission and reliable reconstruction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generative image communication framework based on cross-modal semantic successive refinement. At the transmitter, text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and visual side information compressed by residual vector quantization are transmitted. At the receiver, text and bottleneck features are first fused to predict a base estimate of the intermediate visual representation. The received RVQ indices are then used to recover supplementary visual information and perform residual correction, followed by image reconstruction using a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. During training, a CLIP-based text-image semantic consistency constraint is introduced to preserve the semantic correspondence between generated results and the original text descriptions. During transmission, protection resources are allocated according to the importance of different information branches and RVQ quantization stages. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured underwater acoustic channel records from Watermark show that text and bottleneck features provide complementary semantic and structural conditions, RVQ visual side information further improves reconstruction quality, and layered unequal error protection helps improve recovery at low SNRs. Code-rate allocation experiments reveal a tradeoff between the reliability of fundamental conditions and visual-detail reconstruction under a limited visual-feature coding budget, providing guidance for allocating protection resources in underwater acoustic image transmission.

record.abstract: Abstract A notable achievement of the first generation of JWST surveys was the discovery of an abundance of faint high-redshift (z > 4) broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN) in the Lbol < 1045 erg s−1 regime, previously only accessible at z < 1. The high prevalence of absorption features in their broad hydrogen lines is one of the peculiarities of a significant fraction of this new population. In this paper, we conduct a broad census of Balmer absorption in a sample of 47 Type-1 AGN spanning 2 < z < 7. Accounting for incompleteness of JWST spectroscopic data, we estimate that $44_{-6}^{+21}$ % of Little Red Dots (LRDs) have absorption in Hα while the incidence rate is <25 % (at 2σ) in Little Blue Dots (LBDs). Additionally, R1000 JWST/NIRSpec data is strongly resolution limited, implying an inability to disentangle Doppler broadening in the absorption from optical depth effects. This is alleviated with R2700 observations, although some degeneracies remain. We find a significant correlation between the velocity of the Balmer absorption and the [OIII]5007 narrow line luminosity, suggesting a common driving mechanism. We do not find any other significant correlations (and do not confirm previously claimed correlations) between Balmer absorption and other spectral properties of LRDs (except for the expected correlation between Hα and Hβ absorption velocities). Comparing LRDs, quasars and stellar Hα absorbers, we establish that absorption in both LRDs and broad absorption line quasars is consistent with radiatively driven outflows, echoing the physics of variable stars yet occurring at vastly different scales.

record.abstract: Parallel drafters accelerate LLM decoding by proposing a whole block of draft tokens in a single forward pass, making them attractive for LLM serving. Recent systems optimize goodput (i.e., accepted tokens per second) because rejected drafts steal compute from other requests. However, these systems control only how many tokens are verified, so every request still drafts a full block. At high serving load, we find that drafting consumes up to 40% of step time, of which a majority is discarded because it is never verified. Yet, draft-length control from autoregressive drafters does not carry over, because a parallel drafter commits to its length before its single pass. Moreover, draft and verification lengths are coupled across the batch, so they must be selected jointly for every request while keeping the decision computationally cheap at every step. In this paper, we propose work-conserving speculation (WCS), a design that jointly allocates draft and verification budgets per request in LLM serving, and present ForeSpark as its prototype. ForeSpark realizes WCS with (i) a context-aware pre-draft estimator that predicts acceptance for every candidate length from the target model's context features, (ii) a lightweight joint draft-verify scheduler that selects both lengths through a global sort, and (iii) a post-draft budget distribution that spends verification on the most promising tokens. Implemented on vLLM, ForeSpark improves throughput by up to 1.77x over the state-of-the-art DSpark and by 2.49x over autoregressive decoding at a matched per-request generation rate, without changing the output distribution. It also tolerates higher load, sustaining up to 1.51x the request rate of DSpark under latency service level objectives (SLOs).

record.abstract: Marine surface vehicles (MSVs) have attracted considerable attention for their commercial, scientific, and military applications. Owing to their favorable performance-to-cost ratio, shipboard cameras are widely used to detect and recognize potentially hazardous situations across diverse operational scenarios. However, visual perception is inevitably degraded by restricted conditions, including irregular motion of the imaging platform, adverse weather, and long imaging distances. To improve situational awareness and navigation capabilities, complementary sensors, such as the automatic identification system (AIS), radar, and light detection and ranging (LiDAR), etc., have become essential shipboard equipment. Multi-sensor fusion can provide richer perceptual information and help ensure navigational safety of MSVs in restricted visibility. This article reviews recent progress from intelligent vision to vision-centered multi-sensor fusion for newcomers and researchers in intelligent ship navigation and intelligent waterborne transportation system (IWTS). After introducing the generation of quality-degraded images in restricted visibility, we will review intelligent vision methods for four key issues, i.e., shipboard video stabilization, visual perception enhancement, object detection and tracking, and navigable area segmentation. We then examine vision-centered multi-sensor fusion methods, including infrared-visible image fusion, radar-vision fusion, LiDAR-vision fusion, AIS-vision fusion, and other multi-sensor fusion scenarios. Open-source datasets and safety-critical applications are also summarized and discussed. Finally, we highlight open challenges and future research directions. The collected maritime datasets are available at https://github.com/MAPGroup/Datasets and will be regularly updated.

record.abstract: Walling specification in North-East Nigeria proceeds largely on grounds of cost and familiarity rather than measured environmental or thermal evidence, and the embodied and operational burdens of the choice are conventionally assessed in separate literatures. Criteria were min-max normalised and aggregated using analytic hierarchy process weights, with robustness tested across six weighting scenarios. Transmittance discriminated poorly, the four U-values spanning only thirteen per cent, whereas the dynamic characteristics separated the materials sharply: the hollow sandcrete section returned a time lag of 5.9 hours and a decrement factor of 0.592 against 8.9 hours and 0.331 for CSEB. Embodied carbon ranged from 10.7 kg CO₂e m⁻² for adobe to 118.4 for burnt clay brick, driven almost entirely by clamp-kiln firing. CSEB reduced annual cooling demand by 12.2 per cent and discomfort intensity by 23.1 per cent relative to the control. record.abstract: Abstract The information we hold in mind with working memory (WM) may propagate beyond the cortex and out to the peripheral motor system. For instance, directionally biased hand and eye movements can express simple visuo-spatial features during WM maintenance. If such sensorimotor inflections are a form of WM representation, they may also express more multifaceted and task-adaptive information than just spatial location. Here, we ask whether gaze patterns carry item-specific detail about complex stimuli held in mind, and whether gaze prospectively adapts to the behavioral task demands. To do this, we tracked human eye movements (male and female) during WM for naturalistic images, and we manipulated which image features were most task-relevant (visual or semantic). In two experiments, we found that the eyes moved in complex, item-specific spatiotemporal sequences during WM maintenance. Delay period gaze patterns retraced the scanpaths from stimulus encoding, echoing the ‘gaze reinstatement’ that aligns with neural pattern reactivation during long-term memory retrieval. Therefore, gaze patterns during WM may reinstate visual encoding processes for maintenance. We also used time-resolved representational similarity analyses, guided by convolutional neural network modeling, to test the specificity of WM gaze patterns across a trial. We found that gaze representations were more distinct when the task prioritized visual detail, and also ramped up in anticipation of the WM probe. Therefore, oculomotor WM signals are malleable to when and how the content will be used. These results suggest that the earliest levels of visual processing reflect prospectively-oriented and functionally flexible WM content representations. Significance The eyes are an outwardly accessible extension of the brain. They are the first stop for visual processing, but may also offer a rich window into underlying cognition. For instance, pupil dilation can reflect changing cognitive load, and eye movement biases can reflect basic spatial information about content held in mind with working memory. Working memory is a critical neuro-cognitive function, but its physiological bases remain under debate. Here, we show that eye movements code for more than simple spatial WM, and instead express intricate patterns that read out the complex, real-world stimuli held in mind. This work shows how cognitive states influence oculomotor functions, and also advances theories of WM representation to include the earliest stages of sensory processing.

record.abstract: We construct a quantum measurement protocol for estimating the Rényi entanglement asymmetry, which quantifies symmetry breaking at the level of a subsystem and provides a probe of the quantum Mpemba effect. The protocol combines the SWAP test with a charge-resolving procedure based on randomized symmetry rotations. For a fixed additive accuracy $ε$, the required number of measurements scales as $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ without explicit dependence on the total system size, making the protocol particularly attractive for quantum many-body systems and lattice quantum field theories. As a representative application, we study the quantum Mpemba effect in the lattice Schwinger model with a $θ$ term using classical state-vector simulations. We further estimate the resources required to implement the protocol on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs), and a representative early-FTQC architecture. Our results provide a measurement-efficient framework for investigating anomalous symmetry-restoration dynamics in quantum many-body systems and quantum field theories.

record.abstract: A bstract The logarithm of the time-evolution operator has been termed Magnusian, on account of the fact that its expansion describes the Magnus series. The diagrammatic expansion and computation of the classical Magnusian have been completely established in terms of tree graphs and their Hopf algebra. In this work, we advance the loop expansion further by providing an efficient diagrammatic algorithm to calculate the weight factor of each graph in the quantum Magnusian, known as the Murua coefficient. This is achieved by incorporating two complementary perspectives on the Magnusian at the same time: the color basis and the black-and-white basis. We extract the Murua coefficients from the Magnus series by utilizing these two bases while implementing an exponentiated Wick contraction. In turn, we identify the loop-level extension of Murua’s recursive formula. Eventually, we establish a set of edge-contraction rules which facilitate a direct recursive computation of the Murua coefficients at the purely diagrammatic level, without referencing or directly manipulating the underlying Magnus expansion. record.abstract: The discrepancy between early- and late-Universe determinations of the Hubble constant may point to physics beyond $Λ$CDM or to unaccounted-for systematics. Numerous late-time modifications to the expansion history have been proposed to alleviate this discrepancy, with limited success. Recent works have shown that, when the sound-horizon and supernova calibrations are held fixed, any purely late-time resolution requires a violation of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR). Recasting the tension in the $r_d$-$M_B$ plane, we show explicitly that distance duality, together with BAO and uncalibrated supernova data and a fixed sound-horizon calibration, determines $H_0$ independently of the late-time expansion history. We then test the viability of the required CDDR violation by separately constraining reciprocity violation and photon number non-conservation, deriving a new constraint on reciprocity-violating distortions of angular-diameter distances from BAO and cosmic-chronometer data. Combining this result with existing photon-number-conservation constraints, we find that the level of distance-duality violation needed to resolve the tension is strongly disfavoured by current data. We therefore conclude that, for fixed sound-horizon and supernova calibrations, no modification confined to the late-time expansion history -- even one violating distance duality -- can resolve the Hubble tension, pointing instead toward early-Universe physics or unresolved local systematics.

We develop bandwidth selectors for Dirichlet kernel estimators of densities and projected first derivatives for compositional data. record.abstract: Existing generative model-based approaches to linear inverse problems typically use the acquired noisy measurement to condition or guide sampling in the image domain. In this work, we introduce Dual Flow, a novel joint flow model for solving linear inverse problems by jointly estimating the clean image and its corresponding noise-free measurement from the observation. Specifically, Dual Flow formulates image reconstruction and measurement denoising as a coupled estimation problem, using coupled flows in the image and measurement domains. The acquired noisy measurement $\mathbf{y}_0$ is used only to initialize the measurement state; thereafter, the image and measurement states are jointly updated based on their current values. By construction, the final image and measurement estimates are guaranteed to satisfy the underlying forward model. We derive the sampling updates for the joint flow and show that they are governed by the conditional mean of the clean image given the current joint state. We further derive a closed-form expression for a sufficient statistic of the joint state and show that the required conditional mean can be obtained by solving an image-domain Gaussian denoising problem involving operator-dependent, correlated noise. We train a velocity-prediction network using this formulation to estimate the conditional mean from the derived sufficient statistic. Dual Flow requires no hyperparameter tuning beyond selecting the number of inference steps and achieves substantially shorter reconstruction times than competing methods. Extensive experiments across various linear inverse problems and image datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both distortion metrics and perceptual quality. Additional analyses assess robustness to model mismatch, as well as the ability to generate diverse plausible reconstructions and characterize reconstruction uncertainty.

record.abstract: Innovative intersection designs can improve roadway safety and operational efficiency, but their uncommon geometries may create challenges for driver comprehension during early deployment. Evaluating these designs through full-scale field implementation can also be costly. This paper presents InterSim, a Unity game engine-based human-in-the-loop (HITL) driving simulator that constructs digital twins of site-specific innovative intersections in a virtual environment. InterSim links the real world and the simulation world through two closed cycles: a digital twin cycle that builds each intersection twin from agency design and traffic data and returns evidence from simulation to the agency, and an HITL cycle in which human drivers or automated driving algorithms operate the ego vehicle under identical scenario conditions. The research capabilities of InterSim are demonstrated through two case studies: a surrogate safety study compares post-encroachment time distributions between a Reduced Conflict Intersection and a standard intersection under different traffic volumes; an eco-driving study compares human drivers with a rule-based agent using vehicle-to-infrastructure information and reveals differences in emission and driving behavior. These studies demonstrate that InterSim provides a reusable digital twin platform for investigating innovative intersection designs from diverse perspectives. Demo video and open-source code can be accessed at https://purduedigitaltwin.github.io/InterSim/

record.abstract: Drug discovery requires continuous scientific decision-making across a vast research space. We introduce PharmAgents2, an autonomous system for end-to-end drug discovery that combines knowledge-enhanced decision-making with organized large-scale exploration. Paper2Skill extracts transferable scientific decision knowledge from public sources and, together with expert-developed skills, supports research decisions. Self-Scaling Discovery expands exploration through parallel agents inheriting research context and decision-making capabilities across targets, scientific hypotheses, and discovery strategies. We introduce PharmAgents-Bench v0.1, comprising 121 questions across nine decision scenarios and three end-to-end tasks assessed with expert-defined process rubrics. PharmAgents2 outperforms evaluated baselines in most decision categories and achieves the highest process scores on all three end-to-end tasks. In three real-world studies, autonomous investigations generated findings subsequently supported by human-executed experiments. For LpxH, PharmAgents2 hypothesized a previously unreported allosteric site and screened compounds against it, identifying a novel inhibitor scaffold with experimentally confirmed inhibitory activity and binding. For JAK1, it prioritized a covalent inhibition strategy and nominated compounds with experimentally demonstrated activity. Starting from a known bioactive molecule, Self-Scaling Discovery explored candidate targets across the proteome and identified a new binding target, with the interaction subsequently confirmed experimentally. PharmAgents2 represents a prototype of a virtual pharmaceutical company, marking a step toward autonomous end-to-end drug discovery.

record.abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicle (EV) adoption in Thailand has increased demand for charging infrastructure, particularly at high-density residential buildings with parking and electrical-capacity constraints. This study evaluates the techno-economic feasibility of installing two 60 kW DC chargers and two 22 kW AC chargers at a condominium in Bangkok, with an initial investment of THB 1,990,500 excluding VAT. The assessment integrates project quotations, site-specific electrical designs, charger specifications, and scenario-based financial modeling. Technical feasibility was assessed based on installation requirements, electrical compatibility, and safety provisions, while economic feasibility was evaluated using net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR), and simple payback period (PB). The proposed configuration satisfied the specified technical requirements. Three utilization scenarios considered DC charging for 4–6 h/day and AC charging for 10–14 h/day. Electricity costs were modeled at THB 4.50/kWh, with additional increases of 2.5% and 5% and corresponding adjustments to charging prices. A 10-year project lifetime and a 5.5% discount rate were assumed. The results showed NPVs ranging from THB 382,947.62 to THB 3,527,186.83, IRRs from 9.34% to 34.94%, and PBs from 2.72 to 6.32 years. The best-performing scenario, with DC and AC utilization of 6 and 14 h/day, respectively, achieved an NPV of THB 3,527,186.83, an IRR of 34.94%, and a PB of 2.72 years. Charger utilization, particularly DC utilization, was a key determinant of economic viability. Mixed AC/DC charging infrastructure may therefore be economically attractive under the modeled conditions, although the utilization assumptions were not validated using long-term measured charging-demand data.

record.abstract: The Poisson Nernst Planck (PNP) equation is widely used to simulate ion channel transport, but its strong nonlinearity and coupling characteristics make numerical solutions extremely challenging, and decoupling methods are usually required. The Gummel iteration method is widely adopted as a common decoupling algorithm owing to its simplicity, ease of implementation, and applicability even under complex conditions. But its convergence efficiency highly depends on the selection of the relaxation parameter, unsuitable parameters will lead to slow convergence or even divergence. At present, parameter selection relies heavily on manual experience, which is inefficient and unstable, significantly hindering the solving efficiency for practical problems such as ion channel simulations. To address this, we propose a machine learning-based parameter selection method, which can select near-optimal relaxation parameters for the Gummel iteration of PNP equations for ion channels. Based on the machine learning-based parameter selection algorithm, we develop a coupled finite element and Gummel iteration solver, and more stable convergence and higher computational efficiency have been achieved in ion channel simulations. To validate the method, we conduct tests on two real channels with complex geometries that differ significantly from the training samples. Numerical results demonstrate that this method has a significant effect on improving the convergence efficiency and stability of Gummel iteration, confirming its applicability in practical ion channel simulations.

record.abstract: Next-generation wireless networks are increasingly large-scale, heterogeneous, and dynamic, posing significant challenges to network modeling and control. Digital twins offer a promising solution, but existing approaches typically rely on static models and decouple twin construction from network orchestration, limiting adaptability. Meanwhile, large language models (LLMs) provide strong reasoning capabilities but struggle with graph-structured data and are highly sensitive to prompt design, making inference unreliable. In this paper, we propose Janus, an agentic LLM-based framework that unifies digital twin construction and network orchestration within a closed-loop system. At the core of Janus is a novel NetTwin agent, which introduces a new one-agent, two-role paradigm, enabling a single agent to simultaneously construct the digital twin from partial observations while performing task-driven network decision-making. To realize this, we design a modular architecture with three functional roles, including planner, modeler, and coder, along with a newly designed unified prompt module that further enhances graph reasoning robustness. Extensive evaluations on wireless networks with up to 200 nodes and two representative tasks, including user association and SAGIN routing, show that Janus achieves over 90% digital twin accuracy and near-optimal performance with gaps within 10.53%, while maintaining moderate computational overhead. These results demonstrate the effectiveness, scalability, and generalizability of Janus, paving the way for AI-native autonomous wireless network orchestration.

record.abstract: Promptable perception, from GroundingDINO to Rex-Omni, puts one model behind one prompt interface and returns coordinates for any localisation task. Every model in that line was built for photographs; none has been given a sketch. We present Sketch-Omni, to our knowledge the first perception MLLM built to work on sketches and from them. On a sketch, the sketch is the image, and text prompts detect, point, resolve object and spatial referring expressions, and ground affordances in it. From a sketch, the sketch is the prompt, and a drawing of one object localises that object in a photograph, even among several of the same category, a query that neither a category name nor a photo exemplar can pose. Two obstacles stand in the way. A photo-trained model's attention is tuned to colour and texture, which a sketch does not have, and no dataset pairs a drawing with the one instance it depicts among others of its kind. We build the training data instead of collecting it. An edge detector turns every labelled photograph into a sketch-like drawing that keeps the photograph's labels, and two constructions produce sketch-to-photo instance pairs from existing data. On top of this, photo-guided relation alignment passes each photograph and its edge sketch through the same model and trains the sketch pass to reproduce how the photograph pass relates phrases to patches and patches to each other. Not one training label is drawn by hand. Sketch-Omni reaches 91.4 F1 on sketch-prompted localisation against 81.8 for the strongest general-purpose MLLM, with a lead that doubles when the photograph holds several instances of the queried category, and it is best in 39 of 40 evaluation cells across six tasks. Code, model, and a hand-annotated benchmark of 2754 sketch-to-photo links will be released.

record.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Inherited ataxias are clinically diverse neurodegenerative diseases, complicating the choice of outcome measures for trials. In spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA), regulatory concerns about the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) caused a shift toward functional SARA (f-SARA), contributing to pivotal trial failure. We investigated whether the Upright Stability Score (USS), validated in Friedreich ataxia (FRDA), retains its psychometric properties in SCA, and how it compares with SARA, f-SARA, and the Friedreich Ataxia Activities of Daily Living scale (FA-ADL). METHODS: Cross-sectional data from ambulatory participants in two large international natural-history studies (CRC-SCA and UNIFAI) were analyzed with correlation-based psychometric methods, comparing score distributions across scales and genotypes. RESULTS: Data from 406/343 participants in CRC-SCA/UNIFAI were analyzed. In SCA, the USS captured a wider spectrum of balance performance, while in FRDA, early proprioceptive deficits-particularly impaired stance with eyes closed-constrained score variability. USS correlated strongly with SARA, f-SARA, and FA-ADL in both cohorts. SARA showed moderate skew, and f-SARA showed pronounced floor effects in mildly affected SCA, whereas USS and FA-ADL preserved discrimination at the low end. FA-ADL distributions were broadly comparable across genotypes. INTERPRETATION: USS showed cross-sectional convergent validity with established measures across ambulatory FRDA and SCA, reflecting perceived disease burden (FA-ADL) at least as well as SARA. f-SARA is poorly discriminating in ambulatory SCA and is unlikely to work as an outcome measure, in particular in early cohorts. USS showed the potential to serve as a primary outcome assessment in pivotal SCA trials, but longitudinal evidence is required. Limitations include cross-sectional design and a substantial age difference between cohorts.

record.abstract: Abstract Understanding the sources and evolution of cosmic reionization remains a central challenge in astrophysics, with the escape of ionizing Lyman-continuum (LyC) photons from early galaxies representing a major uncertainty. In this work, we use more than 35,000 galaxy realisations from the thesan-zoom cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations to identify indirect diagnostics of the LyC photon escape fraction (fesc) and the LyC photon escape rate ($\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc}$) across the redshift range z = 3 − 16. We train random forest regression models using these diagnostics to predict both quantities. We present four models: two trained with the full set of simulation-derived indicators to predict fesc and $\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc}$, and two restricted to observables accessible to JWST photometric surveys. We find the 10-to-100 Myr star-formation rate ratio (SFR10/SFR100) and the gas-to-stellar mass ratio (Mgas/M*) to be the strongest diagnostics of fesc, suggesting a strong relationship between ionizing photon escape and gas clearing through bursty star formation. In contrast, rest-frame UV (1500 Å) absolute magnitude (MUV) dominates $\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc}$ prediction. Motivated by the strong predictive power of MUV, we combine observed UV luminosity functions with derived $\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc} - M_\mathrm{UV}$ relations to construct histories of reionization. These are consistent with observational constraints, avoiding the recently reported crisis in the ionizing photon budget. Our analysis suggests that the bulk of reionization occurred rapidly after z ≈ 8, driven by UV-bright galaxies, with the MUV < −17 populations providing the dominant contribution.

record.abstract: Determining centrality of heavy-ion collisions with high resolution is essential for event-by-event analyses, in particular for net-proton fluctuation measurements aimed at locating the QCD critical point. Supervised machine-learning approaches rely on labels generated by model and therefore inherit the model dependence of the training target. In this work, we propose an unsupervised method to determine collision centrality based on optimal transport. Each collision is represented by its 1-Wasserstein distances to a fixed set of landmark events chosen to cover the measured multiplicity range. A point-cloud network trained by contrastive learning then compresses these distances into a compact event embedding, which is partitioned into equal-size centrality classes. We find that this approach groups events with similar $N_{\rm part}$ and yields a better centrality resolution, quantified by the normalized width of the $N_{\rm part}$ distribution, than the conventional method of cutting on particle multiplicity. The method, however, encounters a bottleneck once realistic kinematic cuts are applied to the particles. We attribute this degraded performance to the loss of distinct features between central and peripheral collisions because of applying kinematic cuts. The application of optimal transport to centrality determination in experimental data, remains an open problem that needs further study.

record.abstract: Continual model updating has become a common practice in the deployment of machine learning systems. However, the dynamic training behaviors give rise to new risks not sufficiently addressed by existing studies. In this paper, we present the first systematic study of temporal privacy risk in continually updated deep learning models. We formalize the notion of temporal membership in continually updated models. We then define the temporal membership inference attack, which seeks to infer whether and when individual samples were involved in model training, at both timestamp-level and interval-level granularities. To this end, we propose TMIA, a novel black-box attack that leverages bidirectional LSTMs to infer temporal membership from model outputs observed across successive updates. Through extensive experiments on three language models and three image classification models, we show that TMIA is highly effective and significantly outperforms existing baselines. Finally, we evaluate three potential defenses, revealing the trade-off between privacy protection and model utility.

record.abstract: It is often understood that supernova (SN) feedback in galaxies is responsible for regulating star formation (SF) and generating gaseous outflows. However, a detailed look at the small-scale effects of SNe on the interstellar medium (ISM) in simulations shows that the macroscopic processes of SF suppression and outflow generation proceed in distinct channels. We demonstrate this finding in two independent simulations of isolated dwarf galaxies with very high (m_gas ~ Msun) numerical resolution, LYRA and RIGEL. Our findings suggest that the macroscopic effect of a given SN on the galaxy is best predicted by its local density. Outflows are primarily linked to SNe in diffuse regions expanding to their cooling radii on large (~kpc) scales, while dense SF regions are disrupted in a localized (~pc) manner. However, these separate feedback channels are only distinguishable at very high resolutions capable of following mass scales ^2 . When averaging on coarser scales, ISM densities are greatly mis-estimated, and variations between different SF and SNe-affected regions are severely washed out. It therefore cannot be self-consistently determined, from coarse-resolution information alone , (1) whether a SN tends to contribute to outflows or direct SF suppression, and (2) the rate of SF in a given region. In particular, commonly used parameters in coarse-resolution (subgrid) models, such as the SN cooling radius and SF density threshold, may require more detailed treatments informed by high-resolution studies.

record.abstract: Accurate forecasting of renewable generation requires not only point predictions but also reliable estimates of the uncertainty attached to them, particularly at extended horizons. Machine learning models are increasingly used to predict solar output, but they typically report a single value and capture the associated uncertainty poorly. The standard remedy is to train a model to predict the parameters of an assumed probability distribution directly. Here we develop an alternative two-stage method, motivated by synthetic solar signal generation, in which the forecast error is modeled separately from the expected irradiance. A first long short-term memory (LSTM) network predicts the expected global horizontal irradiance, and a second network models the distribution of the forecast error, which is added back to the mean to give both the forecast and its uncertainty. Using historical weather data from the National Solar Radiation Database and a probability integral transform evaluation, we show that explicitly modeling the error brings the predicted standard deviation markedly closer to the historical value, reducing the deviation between the two by 34.6 percent for a standalone LSTM and by 56.5 percent when the LSTM is coupled to Gaussian process regression, the most reliable of the configurations tested. Because the method models the total forecast error directly, it captures the full predictive uncertainty that matters for decisions, rather than only the model contribution that dropout-based approaches estimate.
